u>0$, $\chi_0\in\mathbb R$, and $a,b, eta\ge0$. Building on earlier results on global existence, boundedness, persistence, and stabilization, we take $\chi_0$ as the bifurcation parameter and examine the effects of $ eta$ and the domain size on the bifurcation.
  Center manifold reduction yields a coefficient $ eta_{n_0}$ at a simple bifurcation mode $n_0$ of a positive constant equilibrium. The pitchfork bifurcation is supercritical if $ eta_{n_0}>0$ and subcritical if $ eta_{n_0}<0$. Stronger desensitization raises the sensitivity required for loss of linear stability. Bifurcation may be supercritical for small $ eta$ but is always subcritical for sufficiently large $ eta$. Thus, desensitization makes patterns harder to trigger and favors abrupt rather than continuous emergence. The bifurcation mode increases with domain size, allowing more complex spatial patterns.
  Under suitable conditions, we prove unbounded continuation of local bifurcation branches. We also show that large-sensitivity stationary sequences satisfying a peak-gap hypothesis develop spike-like profiles. Numerical continuation and time-evolution experiments illustrate the bifurcating branches and spike-like solutions and suggest unbounded continuation and increasingly sharp stationary profiles.

papers.title: A Physical-Space Approach to Modified Scattering for the 3D Hartree Equation: Full-Space and Robin Half-Space
papers.abstract: We prove global well-posedness and modified scattering for the three-dimensional Hartree equation for small data in $H^{0,k}$, with $k>\frac12$ on $\mathbb R^3$ and $k=1$ on the half-space $\mathbb R^3_+$ with a real Robin boundary condition. For these data, the nonlinear and asymptotic analysis is carried out entirely in physical space, combining slow-growth estimates for Galilean vector fields with a scale-invariant interaction estimate. For the half-space problem, we construct an extension intertwining the Robin and free flows and a boundary-adapted field that overcome the loss of normal Galilean symmetry.

papers.title: The Brezis-Nirenberg-type problem for critical cooperative and non-cooperative elliptic systems with general subcritical perturbations
papers.abstract:
We study the Brezis--Nirenberg-type problem for a class of critical cooperative and non-cooperative elliptic systems with general subcritical perturbations. The system couples two equations through a matrix whose off-diagonal entries may be of either sign, a critical Sobolev-type nonlinearity, and a perturbation that may change sign.The main difficulties are threefold: the linear part is governed by a matrix, the critical nonlinearity couples the two components, and the perturbation is general and may change sign.
  We prove an abstract existence result under the energy threshold condition and verify this condition in two regimes. For $N\ge4$ the condition holds for every admissible triple, in both the unperturbed and the perturbed case; the proof uses a new $L^{q}$ estimate for the normalized Aubin--Talenti functions, which controls the negative part of the perturbation. For $N=3$ the eficit in the Sobolev quotient is only of order $\eps^{1/2}$, so a stronger linear threshold condition is required; we establish it explicitly for a ball and, for a general bounded smooth domain, in terms of an abstract constant from the classical Brezis--Nirenberg theory. We also establish the system Sobolev inequality with the same constant as in the scalar case. Since the unperturbed case is included, our results extend the classical theory to cooperative and non-cooperative critical systems with general lower-order perturbations.

papers.title: A class of sum Hessian quotient equations arising in conformal geometry
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence result of $(n-1)$-admissible solutions to a class of sum Hessian quotient equations with the modified Schouten tensor on Riemannian manifolds. By establishing uniform a priori estimates, we prove the solvability of the problem via degree theory.

papers.title: A Quantitative Hydrodynamic Limit for the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck/Navier-Stokes System in the Fine Particle Regime
papers.authors: Zhendong Fang, Jian Li, Kunlun Qi, Huanyao Wen
papers.abstract: We justify the hydrodynamic limit of the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation coupled with the incompressible Navier--Stokes equation in the fine regime with a quantitative convergence rate. In this regime, the limiting dynamics is described by the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier-Stokes system for the fluid-particle mixture. In contrast with the existing relative entropy approaches, the present work extends to a pointwise convergence of the hydrodynamic limits with an explicit rate on any given time interval [0,T]. The proof is based on a Macro-Micro decomposition around the moving local Maxwellian, together with an $\varepsilon$-weighted energy-dissipation structure adapted to the fine particle relaxation scales. Furthermore, we remove the classical small background restriction inherent in high-order energy methods, allowing the limiting profile to be possibly large. This is accomplished by exploiting a hidden Kelvin-Voigt type damped wave equation structure within the macroscopic velocity error system, yielding the critical extra dissipation required to close the uniform estimates.

papers.title: Rigidity for formally determined point source scattering for an anisotropic acoustic medium
papers.abstract: Consider an acoustic medium, occupying three dimensional space, whose anisotropic sound speed is modeled by a Riemannian metric which is Euclidean outside a compact region $D$. The medium is probed by acoustic waves generated by a finite number (dimension dependent) of point sources outside $D$ and the medium response is measured on the boundary of $D$ for a finite time period. We show that if these measurements agree with that of an Euclidean metric then the metric is Euclidean up to a diffeomorphism. This result is similar to the result in \cite{ORS26a} where they used plane waves instead of point sources. Using point sources instead of plane waves presents new difficulties, dealt with in this article.

papers.title: Time Delay of KPP Fronts Across a Semipermeable Barrier
papers.abstract: We study a KPP reaction--diffusion equation on the real line with a semipermeable barrier at the origin, where the flux is continuous and the density jump is proportional to the spatial derivative. With diffusion and linear growth normalized to one, let $\beta$ denote the barrier resistance. For initial data equal to one sufficiently far to the left and zero near the barrier and on the receiving side, we prove convergence on the receiving side to a minimal-speed wave with a unique phase in the Bramson frame. The difference between distant first-arrival times with and without the barrier therefore has a finite limit $\tau_\beta$, independent of the arrival level and continuous in $\beta$. For concave KPP reactions, this delay is strictly increasing in $\beta$ and satisfies $\tau_\beta=K\beta+o(\beta)$ as $\beta\downarrow0$, with $K>1/4$. Without the concavity assumption, the strong-barrier expansion is $\tau_\beta=\frac12\log\beta-\frac12\log\log\beta+C+o(1)$, where $C$ is determined by the homogeneous reference amplitude and the closed donor-side Neumann evolution. The analysis relates the sustained interface input to the front phase through leading-edge estimates, interior matching, and parameter-uniform moment bounds.

papers.title: Directional delays and singular strong-barrier limits for Fisher--KPP propagation across a semipermeable interface
papers.abstract: We study Fisher--KPP propagation from compactly supported data across a planar semipermeable interface in $N\ge2$ dimensions, with unit diffusion and $f'(0)=1$. For every finite resistance, the receiving front has speed $2$ and logarithmic correction $-(N+2)\log t/2$. Its phase is determined by a positive directional amplitude on the closed receiving hemisphere. This amplitude is jointly continuous in resistance and direction and is H\"older continuous in direction with exponent $1/3$. It also determines a threshold-independent signed arrival-time difference. Under concavity, the amplitude decreases strictly with resistance. As the resistance $\beta$ tends to infinity, the amplitude is asymptotic to $2(4\pi)^{-N/2}I_N(\theta)(\log\beta)/\beta$ uniformly on each fixed receiving cone bounded away from the equator. Here $I_N$ is a weighted input moment of the closed Neumann donor problem. Although this moment diverges logarithmically near the equator, the equatorial amplitude tends to half the amplitude of the even Neumann donor solution. The strong-resistance and equatorial limits therefore do not commute. The proof combines critical derivative moments, an integrated Robin trace estimate, Cartesian leading-edge limits, and matching through the wave displacement. The phase and asymptotic formulas require only the smooth KPP assumptions, without the additional restriction $f'\le f'(0)$. Concavity is used for strict resistance ordering and the strict bounds on the limiting equatorial delay.

papers.title: Higher-order necessary conditions for nonscattering
papers.abstract: We study the scattering of incident waves by a class of planar analytic inhomogeneities with constant refractive index, governed by the Helmholtz equation. We derive an infinite hierarchy of necessary conditions for nonscattering: any complex analytic nonscattering incident wave must satisfy infinitely many differential constraints at a specific point determined by the geometry of the inhomogeneity. As an application, we show that for any noncircular elliptical inhomogeneity, every single separated (Mathieu) mode necessarily scatters. This is in stark contrast to the circular case, where single separated (Bessel) modes are nonscattering at infinitely many wavenumbers.

papers.title: Turing bifurcation, criticality, and multistability in a nonlocal advection-reaction-diffusion equation
papers.authors: Yui Nagayama, Masaharu Nagayama, Hiroshi Ishii
papers.abstract: This paper considers a nonlocal advection--reaction--diffusion equation with logistic growth. We investigate how the interaction kernel affects the criticality of Turing bifurcations and the associated multistability. We first prove that nonhomogeneous stationary solutions bifurcate from the positive homogeneous stationary solution. Center manifold reduction yields an amplitude equation near the bifurcation point. This equation provides criteria for supercritical and subcritical bifurcations in terms of the Fourier transform of the interaction kernel. We also derive a sufficient condition for subcriticality. This condition can be satisfied by sufficiently localized attractive interactions. Based on these analytical results, we investigate multistability through numerical bifurcation analysis. The numerical results show that the stable homogeneous stationary solution can coexist with stable nonhomogeneous stationary solutions or stable time-periodic solutions.

papers.title: A quantitative Robin P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} theorem for tangential polygons
papers.authors: Changfeng Gui, Yeyao Hu, Qinfeng Li, Hang Yang
papers.abstract: We extend the quantitative Dirichlet theorem of Gui, Hu, and Li \cite{GuiHuLi2026} to Robin torsional rigidity. For every fixed $\beta>0$, we prove that the regular $N$-gon uniquely maximizes Robin torsional rigidity among tangential $N$-gons of prescribed area. Our explicit perimeter deficit bound contains the Dirichlet deficit obtained by Gui, Hu, and Li \cite{GuiHuLi2026} and an additional Robin term that is positive for nonregular tangential polygons. For triangles, we answer the fixed-area optimization problem recorded as open by Keady and Wiwatanapataphee \cite[Appendix A.1.2]{KeadyWiwatanapataphee2016}. We also establish strict monotonicity along equal-area regular polygons as the number of sides increases, with an explicit bound for each consecutive gap. The proof combines mixed Robin--Neumann triangular cells, spectral estimates for angular concavity, and a quantitative scaling estimate.

papers.title: Strict unimodality of the exact time-domain diffuse-light response under a Robin boundary condition
papers.abstract: Time-domain boundary measurements of diffuse light are temporal point-spread functions whose peak position is used as a robust scalar datum in diffuse optical and fluorescence imaging. We consider the exact response generated by a single fluorescent point target in a homogeneous half-space with a Robin boundary condition. The response is a temporal convolution of two diffusion Green-function factors containing a complementary-error-function boundary correction. For every positive diffusion, absorption, depth, and source--target and detector--target distance parameter, and for every nonnegative Robin parameter, we prove that the normalized exact response is a generalized gamma convolution density. Its extension by zero to the negative half-line is bell-shaped. A differentiable small-time expansion, established by sectorial analyticity and Cauchy estimates, together with the sign-change structure of the first two derivatives, excludes tangential critical points and yields a unique peak with strict increase before it and strict decrease after it. The argument is exact and requires no large-distance, source--detector balance, symmetry, restricted-time, or small-parameter assumption. The same conclusion holds after convolution with an exponential fluorescence-lifetime density for every positive lifetime. The key ingredients are an explicit Stieltjes representation of the Robin factor, hyperbolic complete monotonicity, closure of the generalized gamma convolution class, and bell-shape theory. A derivation of the exact half-space model and the differentiated endpoint asymptotics are included in two appendices.

papers.title: Lifetime-unified quadratic and cubic approximations of fluorescence peak time for a time-domain diffuse-light response
papers.abstract: We study the temporal maximum of a boundary response generated by a coupled diffusion system in a half-space with Robin boundary conditions and a point fluorophore. The fluorescence lifetime enters through a one-sided exponential time convolution. Previous peak-time approximations were derived under separate short- and long-lifetime scalings. We construct a single reduced peak-time formula for every positive ratio of lifetime to the intrinsic width of the transport peak, thereby describing the transition between these regimes without switching formulas. Starting from a known large-distance approximation of the zero-lifetime response, we normalize at its unique maximum and approximate its logarithm quadratically. The resulting scalar mode equation has a unique solution, expressed through the inverse scaled complementary error function. Its endpoint expansions recover the leading structures of the earlier approximations in the corresponding joint large-distance regimes. A cubic correction accounts for the leading local asymmetry. Under a stated bound on the normalized cubic coefficient, we prove uniqueness of its positive mode and agreement with the exact reduced-profile peak expansion through second order in the lifetime. A conditional peak-location stability estimate is combined with a decomposition into transport-profile and local truncation errors. Numerical comparisons with the full diffusion response support the accuracy of the construction. The lifetime-unified formula is distinguished from the fixed-geometry, infinite-lifetime limit, in which the transport tail yields a different peak-time growth law.

papers.title: Global Well-Posedness for the 3-D Inviscid Oldroyd-B Model with Fractional Stress Diffusion
papers.authors: Yi Lu, Chen Liang, Zhaoyang Yin
papers.abstract: We study the 3-D incompressible inviscid Oldroyd-B model with fractional stress diffusion \((-\Delta)^\beta\tau\) and without stress damping. For $\beta \in (\frac{1}{2},1)$ and $s\in [2\beta+\frac{1}{2},\frac{5}{2}]$, we establish local well-posedness for initial data $(u_0,\tau_0)$ in \(H^s(\mathbb R^3)\), provided that \(\|(u_0,\tau_0)\|_{H^\beta}\) is bounded and \(\|\Lambda^\beta(u_0,\tau_0)\|_{H^{s-\beta}}\) is sufficiently small. If, in addition, $\beta\in(\frac{1}{2},\frac{5}{6}]$, we give a global well-posedness result. Our results complement the work of Constantin, Wu, Zhao and Zhu \cite{ConstantinWuZhaoZhu2021} by treating the Sobolev regularity $s\in[2\beta+\frac12,\frac{5}{2}]$, below the threshold $s>\frac52$ considered there. We also provide an $\ell^2$ alternative to the high-frequency $\ell^1$ summability condition in the framework of Wu and Zhao \cite{WuZhao2022}.

papers.title: On micro-macro derivation of traffic flow models with $(A,B)$-connection and its stability
papers.authors: F. Ancona, P. Cardaliaguet, A. Cesaroni
papers.abstract: We show that $(A,B)$-connections for conservations laws with a flux discontinuity can be obtained as limits of perturbed Follow-the-Leader (FtL) models, and provide continuity and surjectivity of the map associating the perturbation of the dynamics with the flux limiter.

papers.title: The Bardos-Tartar Conjecture for the Navier-Stokes Equations
papers.authors: Douglas Barnes, Samuel Liew, Edriss Titi
papers.abstract: We consider the incompressible viscous Navier-Stokes equations in dimension $d=2,3$ with periodic boundary conditions and time-independent external forcing. When $d=2$, the Bardos-Tartar conjecture asks whether the set of solutions at any given positive time is dense in the Hilbert subspace of $L^2$ consisting of mean-zero divergence-free vector fields, with respect to the strong $L^2$ norm. We prove the Bardos-Tartar conjecture and, more generally, its analogue for the hyperviscous Navier-Stokes equations studied by Guo-Titi. In addition, for $d=2,3$ we show that any given initial condition is either backwards-extendable (i) for all values of viscosity $\nu>0$, or (ii) only for viscosities that belong to a Lebesgue-null subset of $\mathbb{R}_+$. When (i) holds, we show the initial condition and forcing must be real-analytic (in fact, both belong to $D(e^{\sigma A})$ for some $\sigma>0$, where $A$ is the Stokes operator). Furthermore, we show that (i) is extremely unstable under perturbations. In particular, given any initial condition we show that two Fourier modes can be perturbed so that (ii) holds.

papers.title: Spectral Theory for Schrodinger Operators with Interface Transmission Conditions
papers.authors: Linlin Su, Yantao Wang, Zhannan Zhuang
papers.abstract: Interfaces influence transport across biological membranes, habitat boundaries, and composite media. Motivated by these applications, we study two classes of Schrodinger eigenvalue problems with transmission conditions allowing jumps in the solution or its normal derivative. We develop a weighted variational framework that accommodates asymmetric interface coupling and yields self-adjoint realizations in suitable weighted Hilbert spaces. For both problems and their adjoints, we establish discrete spectra, variational eigenvalue characterizations, and eigenfunction completeness in arbitrary spatial dimensions. We prove spectral continuity and identify limiting spectra in singular parameter regimes. We also extend Courant's nodal domain theorem to eigenfunctions that may be discontinuous across the interface. The spectral results further extend to divergence-form elliptic operators under suitable assumptions on the coefficients. These results provide a foundation for analyzing elliptic and parabolic equations with interface transmission conditions.

papers.title: Interior Regularity for Stable Solutions of Semilinear Elliptic Equations with Sign-Changing Nonlinearities
papers.authors: Long-Han Huang, Yuxuan Zhou, Wenming Zou
papers.abstract: We investigate interior regularity for stable solutions of the semilinear elliptic equation $-\Delta u=f(u)$ in an open set $\Omega\subseteq \mathbb R^n$, where $f$ is locally Lipschitz and may change sign. We establish sharp interior H\"older estimates for stable classical solutions in every dimension $n\le 9$, thereby fully resolving a question raised by Cabr\'e concerning interior regularity without the nonnegativity assumption on $f$. For $n\le 5$, we also give a short alternative proof of the corresponding H\"older regularity result due to Peng, Zhang, and Zhou. We further establish higher-integrability estimates for the gradient and $L^1$ bounds for the Hessian in all dimensions. For $n\ge 10$, we obtain BMO and Morrey estimates, extending related results previously established for nonnegative nonlinearities. When $f$ is convex, we extend the interior regularity estimates to stable weak solutions through an approximation theorem. As applications, we prove Liouville-type theorems for entire stable solutions of equations with sign-changing nonlinearities across all dimensions.

papers.title: Boundary Harnack inequalities for the fractional $p$-Laplacian in Reifenberg flat domains
papers.abstract: We prove a scale-invariant boundary Harnack inequality and H\"older continuity up to the boundary of quotients of positive fractional $p$-harmonic functions in Reifenberg flat domains with sufficiently small flatness constant, for $0<s<1$ and $2\le p<2/(1-s)$. The solutions are globally nonnegative, vanish on a common exterior boundary patch, and belong to the natural local energy and $(p-1)$-tail class. Their distant exterior values may be unrelated and unbounded. After normalization at a corkscrew point, the comparison and H\"older constants depend only on $n,s,p$. We first establish local half-space boundary comparison for every $p\ge2$ and prove relative approximation by the half-space profile in Reifenberg domains. The compactness argument identifies escaped exterior mass and excludes its constant source term. Interior $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity then yields gradient non-degeneracy and lower increment bounds in a cone of directions. To treat the degenerate kernels produced by linearization, we develop estimates for weighted non-local forms and prove a localized Harnack inequality for bounded quotients, retaining the full exterior interactions. Ordered variational deformations and a common fractional $p$-harmonic majorant yield comparison for solutions with unrelated exterior data. Truncation of distant data and fractional $p$-harmonic replacement extend the estimates from the variational energy class to the natural tail class.

papers.title: Recovery of coefficients in a Schr\"{o}dinger system with nonlinear coupling
papers.abstract: We consider the inverse problem of recovering time-dependent coefficients in a system of Schr\"{o}dinger equations with coupled nonlinear terms. We first address the well-posedness of the system for small boundary data and trivial initial data. Then, we show that the linearized Neumann data stably determines the nonlinear coefficients provided that, at any given time, they are known in some neighborhood of the boundary. The proof relies on linearization and complex geometric optics (CGO) solutions for the linear Schr\"{o}dinger equation. We conclude by outlining an approach based on the direct use of Carleman estimates to recover time-independent coefficients in the setting of trivial boundary data but nontrivial initial data.

papers.title: Optimizers for the finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring inequality
papers.abstract: The finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring inequality provides an estimate on the Riesz sum of the first $N$ negative eigenvalues of the fractional Schr\"odinger operator $(-\Delta)^s-V$ in terms of the $L^{\gamma+\frac{d}{2s}}(\mathbb R^d)$ norm of the potential $V$, where the Riesz exponent $\gamma>\max\left\{0,1-d/(2s)\right\}$. We prove the existence of optimizers for every finite rank by establishing a result on the spectrum in the case of dichotomy. We further characterize the spectral gap and qualitative properties of optimizers, including the Euler--Lagrange equation, regularity, and asymptotic behavior at infinity. In particular, under the condition $\gamma+{d}/{(2s)}\geq 3+{4s}/{d}$, we show that all normalized maximizing sequences are precompact modulo translations. Moreover, we derive a strict binding inequality for the optimal constants in the finite-rank setting, which implies that the optimal fractional Lieb--Thirring constant, if it exists, cannot be attained by a potential with finitely many negative eigenvalues.

papers.title: A multi-point maximum principle to prove the global Harnack inequality for the doubly nonlinear heat equation
papers.authors: Ben Andrews, Daniel Hauer, Jessica Slegers
papers.abstract: This work aims to present a new proof of the global pointwise Harnack inequality satisfied by positive viscosity solutions of the doubly nonlinear heat equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Our approach is based on a multi-point maximum principle argument introduced by the authors in a recent article [Calc. Var., 2026]. Required for the proof is a new variation of the maximum principle for semicontinuous functions, which is a standard tool in the analysis of viscosity solutions. In particular, our techniques provide a new proof of the Harnack inequalities satisfied by positive solutions of the porous medium equation and the $p$-heat equation, which were derived by Auchmuty and Bao [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc., 1994] using results of Aronson and B\'enilan [C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris, 1979] and Esteban and V\'azquez [Arch. Rational Mech. Anal., 1988]. The results contained in this article have also been discussed in the third author's doctoral thesis.

papers.title: A sharp criterion for well-posedness of semilinear Schr\"odinger equations on the real line
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for semilinear Schr\"odinger equations on the real line. We establish a sharp necessary and sufficient condition on the nonlinearity for local well-posedness in Sobolev spaces of regularity greater than five halves. This criterion is formulated in terms of the Mizohata condition and is equivalent to explicit algebraic conditions on the nonlinearity. To prove sufficiency, we combine energy estimates with a gauge transformation adapted to the bounded primitive arising from the Mizohata condition. To prove necessity, we show that the failure of the condition yields a dense set of initial data for which no solution exists on any positive time interval.

papers.title: Moment Propagation for the Vlasov--Poisson System with Gyroscopic Forces, Velocity Diffusion, and Specular Reflection
papers.abstract: This paper studies the three-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system with gyroscopic forces and velocity diffusion. For the Cauchy problem in $\mathbb R^3$ and the specular--Dirichlet problem in bounded domains, we prove the propagation of velocity moments of order $k>2$ for weak solutions with bounded $L^1\cap L^{\infty}$ norms and kinetic energy. The proof applies Serre's compensated integrability to weighted mass--momentum tensors to derive density estimates. A finite iteration alternating moment propagation with improved density integrability then closes the estimates. These estimates provide a simplified approach to moment propagation and yield global continuation of classical solutions.

papers.title: On a critical curl-curl system of Lane-Emden type
papers.authors: Ioannis Arkoudis, Jaros{\l}aw Mederski, Andrzej Szulkin
papers.abstract:
We study the system $

We prove the existence of a ground state solution by reducing the system to a quasilinear fourth-order curl-curl equation and minimizing the associated Sobolev-curl quotient. papers.title: Fundamentals of Potential theory for a hypoelliptic process
papers.abstract: This article aims at solving open questions related to the well-posedness of Potential theory objects in a hypoelliptic setting. We provide here the expression of the equilibrium measure, capacity and electrostatic energy between smooth open sets $\A$ and $\B$ for the underdamped Langevin process. Additionally, the capacity is shown to be the solution of two variational principles which extend the well-known Dirichlet and Thomson principles in the hypoelliptic setting. Due to the degeneracy of the operator at hand, the results display significant differences with the standard elliptic setting.

papers.title: Inverse Wave Problems on Graphs
papers.abstract: We study inverse wave problems on finite graphs from time-dependent measurements on a prescribed set of vertices. With the graph geometry known, we consider recovery of either the initial signal or the vertex wave speeds when the other is given. Initial-signal recovery is characterized by observability of the associated finite-dimensional system, while a single experiment determines the vertex wave speeds under a zero forcing condition and a natural nonharmonicity assumption. We establish stability estimates for both recovery problems, develop a nonlinear least-squares reconstruction method, and extend the results to positively weighted graphs. Numerical simulations illustrate the reconstruction and examine the effects of observation geometry, time horizon, coefficient localization, and measurement noise on its performance. Our results are motivated both by numerical approaches to continuous inverse wave problems, where spatial discretization leads naturally to graph-based systems, and by applications in which the underlying dynamics are inherently discrete and evolve on networks.

papers.title: On the uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for the Motsch-Tadmor model
papers.authors: Tamari Kldiashvili, Stefano Rossi, Lara Trussardi
papers.abstract: We consider the Motsch-Tadmor model, a modification of the Cucker-Smale model for flocking dynamics that incorporates asymmetric communication weights. In the case of uniformly positive interactions, we consider the validity problem for the limiting kinetic equation, proving a uniform-in-time propagation of chaos result in the moving frame given by the consensus velocities. The result is obtained by studying the reversibility of the communication weights and by implicitly characterizing the asymptotic consensus.

papers.title: The Calder\'on operator for time-harmonic Maxwell's equations in closed waveguides
papers.abstract: We consider the time-harmonic Maxwell's equations in a closed, cylindrical waveguide with longitudinal invariant but heterogeneous permittivity and permeability. We consider minimal smoothness assumptions, i.e., the material parameters have to be in $L^\infty$ and the cross section has to be Lipschitz with a possibly non-trivial topology. First, we show that the associated Calder\'on operator is well-defined and bounded in the natural trace spaces $\mathbf{H}_0^{-1/2}(\operatorname{curl}_\Gamma;\Gamma) \to \mathbf{H}_0^{-1/2}(\operatorname{div}_\Gamma;\Gamma)$. Second, we consider interior Maxwell problems obtained from using the Calder\'on operator and analyze their well-posedness. Furthermore, we report some additional results on the location and group velocities of the waveguide wavenumbers.

papers.title: Sharp Hessian integrability for the planar Monge--Amp\`ere equation
papers.authors: XiaoRui Lu, Jin Yan, Bao Yu, Yang Zhou
papers.abstract:
We determine the optimal local integrability of the Hessian for planar convex Alexandrov solutions satisfying $$
  \lambda\,dx\leq\mu_u\leq\lambda^{-1}\,dx,
  \qquad 0<\lambda<1. $$ The distributional Hessian satisfies the sharp endpoint estimate $$
  D^2u\in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{P,\infty},
  \qquad
  P=\frac{1+\lambda}{1-\lambda}. $$ This settles the weak estimate proposed by De Philippis and Figalli and identifies the larger optimal exponent $P$. We further construct strictly convex $C^1$ solutions for which the distribution function of the Laplacian is comparable to $T^{-P}$ for all sufficiently large $T$. Hence both the exponent and the weak Lorentz endpoint are optimal: $L^{P,\infty}$ cannot be replaced by $L^{P,b}$ for any finite $b>0$.
  As applications, we obtain sharp estimates in Minty coordinates and optimal quantitative bi-Lipschitz restrictions for gradient maps, including an optimal exceptional-mass bound in quadratic-cost transport.

papers.title: Boundary geometry and concentration points for attractive Bose-Einstein condensates with a ring-shaped potential
papers.authors: Shubin Yu, Chun-Lei Tang, Ziheng Zhang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the ground states of attractive Bose-Einstein condensates in a bounded domain $\Omega\subset \mathbb R^2$ under the ring-shaped trapping potential $$ V(x)=(|x|-1)^2. $$ The boundary geometry of $\Omega$ may allow the ring $\Gamma=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:|x|=1\}$ of global minima for $V(x)$ to meet both the interior and the boundary of $\Omega$. As the interaction strength approaches the critical value, we prove that if $\Gamma\cap \Omega\not=\emptyset$, the mass of ground states concentrates at a point $x_0\in\Gamma\cap \Omega$ that has maximal distance from $\partial\Omega$. Our method relies on exponential upper and lower bounds for the difference between the bounded domain and whole space minimal energies. The essential lower bound follows from a uniform quadratic-growth estimate near the ground state manifold of the whole space problem, which is established by combining the nondegeneracy of the optimizer for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality with a Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction.

papers.title: Existence and classification of solutions for singular 1-Laplacian equations with gradient terms
papers.authors: Antonio J. Mart\'inez Aparicio, Francescantonio Oliva, Francesco Petitta

papers.title: Quantitative vanishing-regularization limits for degenerate cross-diffusion with changing boundary strata
papers.authors: E. Yu. Shchetinin, A. A. Shevchuk, S. I. Salpagarov
papers.abstract: We study a vanishing-regularization limit for a degenerate cross-diffusion system on the simplex when the active boundary stratum of a smooth reference solution may change in space and time. The mobility $M(u)=\operatorname{diag}u-u\otimes u$ loses rank when a component vanishes, so a fixed relative entropy or an unweighted two-point gradient estimate cannot remain uniformly coercive across moving faces. We introduce a geometric-relative framework that separates the single emerging normal direction from the active tangential subsystem. Its ingredients are a global resolvent geodesic distance, a boundary-oriented rank-one perspective correction, an intrinsic Schur-normal De Giorgi alternative, a mean-free tangential iteration with temporal-flux control, and a terminal coupled Schur compactness argument. These mechanisms yield a non-circular first-exit theorem for smooth approximations and then pass to admissibly approximable entropy weak solutions. If the strong solution stays a fixed distance from the codimension-two skeleton and its vanishing components satisfy $|\nabla v_i|\lesssim v_i^{\alpha}$ and $|\{0<v_i<r\}|\lesssim r^{\sigma}$, then the augmented relative energy is bounded by $\rho_\lambda=\lambda^{2\alpha+\sigma}$ if $2\alpha+\sigma<2$, $\rho_\lambda=\lambda^2|\log\lambda|$ if $2\alpha+\sigma=2$, and $\rho_\lambda=\lambda^2$ if $2\alpha+\sigma>2$. For a hypersurface contact $v_i\asymp d^p$, $p\ge2$, this gives $\rho_\lambda=O(\lambda^{2-1/p})$ and $\|u^\lambda-v\|_{L^\infty(0,T;L^2)}=O(\lambda^{1-1/(2p)})$.

papers.title: Global strong solutions without contact for a viscous fluid interacting with a purely elastic beam
papers.abstract: We consider a two-dimensional incompressible viscous fluid confined in a periodic channel between a fixed flat wall and a purely elastic periodic beam. For compatible initial fluid velocity in $H^1$, beam height in $H^3$, and beam velocity in $H^1$, with strictly positive initial height, we establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. In particular, there is no contact of the beam and bottom, which is built on a uniform distance bound derived by the mechanical energy and fluid dissipation through a height-dependent degenerate elliptic regularization of the classical distance test. Combining tangential differentiation, a fractional estimate for the height, and a negative-order tangential estimate for the accelerations, we establish a global regularity estimate. Moreover, quadratic time-weighted estimates that quantify the higher regularity at positive times are justified. As a consequence, the work gives an affirmative answer to the problem proposed by Grandmont and Hillairet (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 220(3): 1283--1333, 2016) of whether fluid dissipation alone is sufficient to derive the distance estimate.

papers.title: Cone Invariance and Homoclinic Standing Waves for Cooperative Finite-Range DNLS Equations
papers.abstract: We develop a constrained-power variational framework for positive homoclinic standing waves in one-dimensional discrete nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with cooperative finite-range interactions. Starting from periodic lattices, we construct constrained energy maximizers and use the associated projected gradient flow to establish positive invariance of the cone of nonnegative, even, and unimodal profiles. A central result is that the monotone ordering of the interaction coefficients, \(a_1\ge a_2\ge\cdots\ge a_M\ge0\), with \(a_1>0\), provides the structural condition ensuring preservation of this cone under finite-range coupling. Under a strict maximum condition above the linear spectral edge, we obtain a uniform frequency gap and period-independent exponential localization. These estimates provide the compactness required for the infinite-period limit and yield positive, even, unimodal, and exponentially localized homoclinic standing waves as strong \(\ell^2(\mathbb Z)\)-limits of periodic constrained maximizers. Numerical computations for several interaction ranges and cooperative kernels illustrate the effects of extended coupling on dispersion and localization and support the periodic-to-homoclinic convergence predicted by the analysis.

papers.title: Transference theory for the trilinear restriction estimate and an application to the quadratic NLS in 3D
papers.authors: Ioan Bejenaru, Vitor Borges, Tiklung Chan
papers.abstract: In this article we develop a theory for effectively transferring trilinear restriction estimates for the Schr\"odinger equation to functions in a more general resolution space adapted to the Schr\"odinger equation. As an application we provide a global theory for the quadratic NLS in three spatial dimensions in the critical Sobolev space $\dot{H}^{-\frac{1}{2}}$.

papers.title: Global well-posedness of the periodic Majda-Biello systems in the resonant case
papers.abstract:
We study the Cauchy problem for the following Majda-Biello system in the resonant case $\alpha \in (0,4]\setminus\{1\}$ on the periodic domain $\mathbb{T}$. \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{rcl}
  u_{t} + u_{xxx} & = & - v v_x,
  v_{t} + \alpha v_{xxx} & = & - (uv)_{x},
  (u,v)|_{t=0} & = & (u_0,v_0), \end{array} \right. \quad x \in \mathbb{T}, \, t \in \mathbb{R}. \] Here, the initial data $u_0$ and $v_0$ live in the Sobolev space $H^{s}(\mathbb{T})$ and $u_0$ has zero mean over $\mathbb{T}$. We establish the optimal global well-posedness for the above system when $s\geq \min\{1, s_\alpha+\}$, where $s_\alpha$ is a constant depending only on $\alpha$, and $s_\alpha = \frac12$ for almost every $\alpha \in (0,4]\setminus\{1\}$. These indices match the sharp ones in the local theory obtained by Oh (Int. Math. Res. Not., 18:3516-3556, 2009). The main novelty of our proof is to introduce a third modified energy in the I-method by performing a partial correction to the second modified energy around the resonant region. This partial correction avoids the singularity in the full correction, and therefore makes it possible to pointwise bound the quintilinear multipliers arising in the time derivative of the third modified energy. Another feature in our proof is the combination of the Diophantine approximation theory with the sparsity of nearly resonant frequency pairs on the periodic lattice to obtain the key quadrilinear and quintilinear estimates, leading to an almost conservation law sufficient for the global iteration.

papers.title: Uniform estimates for elliptic systems with critical Sobolev coefficients
papers.abstract: The $W^{1,p}$ estimate for uniformly elliptic operators of divergence form with VMO coefficients is classical. In particular, this provides $W^{1,p}$ estimates for elliptic operators with coefficients in $W^{1,n}$. However, this theory does not yield constants in the estimates controlled by the $W^{1,n}$ norm of the coefficients, since the total $W^{1,n}$ norm does not control the rate of decay for the mean oscillation. In this work, we establish uniform estimates for divergence-form elliptic systems whose coefficients lie in the critical Sobolev--Lorentz spaces $W^{1,(n,s)}$ with $1\le s<\infty$, have an $L^\infty$-bounded spatially symmetric part, and satisfy an integral ellipticity condition. The constant in the estimate is controlled by the corresponding norms of coefficients and the ellipticity constant.

papers.title: Variance-Feedback Noise in Interacting Diffusions: Shape Dynamics and Mean-Field Limits
papers.abstract: We study a system of $N$ attractive interacting diffusions where the variance feeds back into the noise. That is the common and idiosyncratic Brownian forcing has amplitude $\kappa(S_t^N)^q$, with $S_t^N$ the empirical variance of the system, $\kappa>0$ and $q\geq 0$. With the interaction kernel given by $K(z)=|z|^p z$, for $p\geq 0$, feedback through the empirical variance gives the system critical homogeneity at $q=(p+2)/4$. For this exponent an intrinsic time change separates the variance from the normalized centered configuration: the latter evolves autonomously on a unit sphere and, when it is not purely driven by common noise and the sphere has positive dimension, is a reversible elliptic diffusion with an explicit invariant Gibbs measure. In this case, for $p>0$, the stationary averaged dissipation gives an exact finite-particle trichotomy between consensus, recurrent excursions through arbitrarily small and large variance scales, and finite-time explosion. At critical homogeneity we also derive an autonomous unit-variance mean-field equation and its constrained free-energy dissipation identity. Across the subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes, we establish well-posedness and boundary classifications and prove conditional propagation of chaos on intervals where the limiting solution is unique and nonexplosive. We connect the sharp finite-particle coercivity constants to a mean-field variational problem. Finite-size It\^o corrections enlarge the universal coercive consensus region. We solve the linear model, where $p=0$, completely, including invariant laws, explosion probabilities, noncommuting limits, and an $N^{-1/2}$ transition window.

papers.title: The $(n-1)$-linear restriction estimate in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with degenerate curvature
papers.abstract: We revisit the $(n-1)$-linear restriction estimate in $\mathbb{R}^n$ proved by the first author in \cite{Be-6} and refine the result in the case when the curvature assumptions contain small parameters. The standard $L^p$ estimate is replaced by a more complex norm/quasi-norm of type $\ell^p L^\frac{2}{n-2}$ which reflects the geometry of wave packet propagation and the degenerate curvature assumptions. The primary motivation for this work stems from a concrete application to the study of the quadratic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^{3+1}$, which is done in a companion paper \cite{BeBoCh}.

papers.title: $\lambda$-geodesic convexity of the squared sliced-Wasserstein distance
papers.abstract: The squared Wasserstein distance with respect to a fixed target measure is not a convex function along Wasserstein geodesics over $\mathbb{R}^d$ when $d\geq 2$. Still, in dimension $d=1$, this function is $2$-geodesically convex. We prove that the square of the sliced-Wasserstein distance (which is a distance constructed averaging one-dimensional Wasserstein distances) is $\lambda$-geodesically convex (possibly with $\lambda \leq 0$) on sets of measures satisfying upper bounds on their density, when the target measure satisfies some given geometric conditions. We also present some consequences of this result in the study of the sliced-Wasserstein flow.

papers.title: Functions of bounded variation are not dense in the Strong BD Norm
papers.abstract: We prove that functions of bounded variation are not dense in the space of functions of bounded deformation with respect to the strong BD norm. Using alternating Riesz products and directional slicing, we construct on every nonempty open subset of $\R^n$ ($n\ge2$) a continuous, compactly supported BD function that is at positive distance from BV.

papers.title: Semiclassical Band Splitting in the Infinite Chern Band Model
papers.abstract: We study the two lowest Bloch bands of the infinite Chern band model in the semiclassical limit. When the Berry curvature parameter is an odd multiple of \(\pi\), we derive an explicit asymptotic formula for their exponentially small splitting, uniformly over the Brillouin torus. The proof combines Agmon estimates and WKB approximations for a matrix Schr\"odinger operator whose lowest potential eigenvalue has two wells. Geometric properties of the Agmon distance allow us to compute the leading tunneling coefficients by the method of stationary phase. We provide numerical computations to illustrate the asymptotic formula and support the conjecture that the two bands remain separated for other values of the Berry curvature parameter.

papers.title: A Hybrid High-Order method for variable-exponent Leray-Lions problems with convergence under minimal regularity
papers.abstract: We consider a homogeneous Dirichlet problem for nonlinear elliptic equations in divergence form with Leray--Lions fluxes of variable growth. The class includes the variable-exponent $p(\cdot)$-Laplacian and regularized Carreau--Yasuda-type laws. We propose and analyze a Hybrid High-Order (HHO) discretization on general polytopal meshes, a hybrid nonconforming method based on cell and face polynomial unknowns of arbitrary degree. We develop a variable-exponent polynomial and discrete functional toolkit centered on a mean-exponent norm equivalence, together with inverse, trace, Poincar\'e--Wirtinger, Sobolev--Poincar\'e, discrete Lebesgue embedding, interpolation, and compactness estimates adapted to HHO unknowns. We then establish well-posedness of the nonlinear discrete problem and convergence without assuming additional regularity of the exact solution beyond its natural energy space. The discrete potential converges strongly in every uniformly subcritical variable-exponent Lebesgue space, the reconstructed gradient converges strongly in the natural variable-exponent space, and the stabilization energy vanishes. Numerical experiments in two, three, and four space dimensions confirm convergence for singular solutions and for exponent fields ranging from close to $1$ up to $6$. Quantitative a priori error estimates for the same method are derived in a companion paper.

papers.title: A priori error estimates for a Hybrid High-Order method on variable-exponent Leray-Lions problems
papers.abstract: We derive a priori error estimates for the Hybrid High-Order (HHO) discretization of variable-exponent Leray--Lions problems introduced in a companion convergence study. HHO methods belong to the family of hybrid nonconforming methods, based on cell and face polynomial unknowns of arbitrary degree. Under additional broken regularity of the exact solution and its flux, we establish a localized error estimate that retains the individual element sizes and a global estimate whose rate distinguishes the purely subquadratic, mixed subquadratic--superquadratic, and purely superquadratic regimes. In the subquadratic range, we also derive a regime-dependent refinement that compares the local approximation scale with the local non-degeneracy scale and recovers the optimal polynomial order when that scale is resolved by the mesh. The analysis relies on variable-exponent approximation properties of polynomial projectors, mean-exponent tools for discrete polynomial spaces, and weighted monotonicity estimates. The framework also covers regularized and mildly non-symmetric anisotropic Carreau--Yasuda-type fluxes. Numerical experiments on Cartesian and Voronoi meshes support the predicted rates and show that the regularity assumption on the flux cannot be dispensed with.

papers.title: Backward stochastic porous media equation with polynomial growth
papers.authors: Ioana Ciotir, Dan Goreac, Juan Li, Yufan Peng, Eduard Rotenstein
papers.abstract: We investigate the well-posedness of a backward stochastic porous media equation whose nonlinear term is a polynomial operator corresponding to the slow diffusion regime. The main challenge stems from the structure of this nonlinear operator, which causes the operator to lose maximal monotonicity and prevents the use of standard weak-strong convergence techniques to identify the limit. Moreover, since the Laplace operator makes it difficult to separate the operators and discuss them individually, we attempt to obtain the of limit by investigating the global properties of the operator.

papers.title: Finite Volume Convergence for a Heat Equation with a Measure-Valued Source
papers.authors: Matthias Gobbert, Martin Kru\v{z}\'{\i}k, Andreas Meister, Michael Muscedere
papers.abstract: Past work with Tom Seidman analyzed the spatial convergence order of the numerical finite element method applied to time-dependent diffusion-reaction equations with a measure-valued source term. For smooth source terms, the numerical method has second-order accuracy, but the non-smooth source terms introduce a limitation of the order that depends on the spatial dimension. This work in honor of Tom extends the analysis to the finite volume method in its clas- sical two-point flux form and shows that the regularity of the source term reduces the convergence order to 1 in two and 0.5 in three spatial dimensions which is reduced from the nominal second-order and depends on the space dimension. Computational tests with a point source modeled by a Dirac delta distribution exhibit the behavior predicted by the analytical results.

papers.title: Nonpersistence of full-dimensional tori with polynomial decay in nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
papers.abstract: We establish local nonpersistence of full-dimensional invariant tori with polynomially decaying actions for the periodic quintic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \[ iu_t-u_{xx}+T_vu+\mu|u|^4u=0,\qquad x\in\mathbb T:=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z). \] For every $\kappa\geq1$, we construct a fixed bounded real Fourier multiplier $T_ve^{ijx}=v_je^{ijx}$ whose frequencies $\lambda_j=j^2+v_j$ satisfy the Bourgain-type Diophantine condition \[ \operatorname{dist}\left(\sum_j\ell_j\lambda_j,\mathbb Z\right) \geq\gamma_\kappa\prod_j(1+\ell_j^2\langle j\rangle^{2\kappa})^{-1} \] for some $\gamma_\kappa>0$ and every nonzero finitely supported integer sequence $\ell$, where $\langle j\rangle=\max\{1,|j|\}$. For this multiplier, every $3<M<4\kappa+\frac12$, every $A>0$, and all sufficiently small $\mu A^2>0$, the closed relative action tube of radius $3/10$ around $I_j=A\langle j\rangle^{-M}$ contains no full-dimensional invariant torus in $H^1(\mathbb T)$ carrying a complete flow, with arbitrary frequencies allowed. This advances the study of the polynomial-decay problem identified by Kuksin as a main open problem in KAM theory for one-dimensional Hamiltonian PDEs [Amer. Math. Soc. Transl. Ser. 2, 212 (2004), 237--258, Problem 7.1]. Bourgain discussed a related question for short-range Hamiltonian systems [Russian Math. Surveys 59 (2004), 231--246, Section 3]. The proof combines simultaneous Diophantine and weighted homological estimates, an exact common-phase transformation, and one normal-form step on four adjacent Fourier coordinates. Uniform phase rotation forces an action excursion, while overlapping parameter intervals cover all sufficiently small positive perturbations. The mechanism suggests applications to other Hamiltonian PDEs.

papers.title: Classes of integrable metrics on Banach spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce a large new class of (weak) metrics on the Hardy space that have infinite families of conservation laws in involution. The construction of the metrics and the integrals involve the Hankel operator and a field of Nijehuis operators. The commutativity of the integrals is based on the notion of the coupling transform, which allows us to recursively construct new classes of metrics and integrals. We characterize the spectrum of the Nijenhuis operators. The paper establishes a connection between a rich class of completely integrable geodesic flows appearing in the finite dimensional Riemannian geometry and a new class of integrable systems in Banach spaces.

papers.title: A proof of Onsager's Conjecture for the SQG equation
papers.abstract: We construct solutions to the SQG equation that fail to conserve the Hamiltonian while having the maximal allowable regularity for this property to hold. This result solves the generalized Onsager conjecture on the threshold regularity for Hamiltonian conservation for SQG. We also prove nonuniqueness for arbitrary smooth data and an h-principle result.

papers.title: A quantitative Borg-Levinson theorem for a large class of unbounded potentials
papers.abstract: We prove a quantitative Borg-Levinson theorem for a broad class of unbounded potentials when the spatial dimension is five or greater. In the final section, we outline the modifications required to extend the main result to the anisotropic case.

papers.title: On the dynamics of leapfrogging vortex rings
papers.authors: Martin Donati, Lars Eric Hientzsch, Christophe Lacave, Evelyne Miot
papers.abstract: The evolution of highly concentrated vorticity around rings in the three-dimensional axisymmetric Euler equations is studied in a regime for which the leapfrogging dynamics predicted by Helmholtz is expected to occur. We provide in this paper the first result deriving this phenomenon for a general class of initial data in the suitable regime. The singular interaction of rings requires significant improvements of weak and strong localization estimates obtained in prior works. Our method is based on the combination of a new variational argument and a recently introduced double iterative procedure.

papers.title: Lipschitz regularity of fractional $p$-Laplacian
papers.abstract: In this article, we investigate the H\"{o}lder regularity of the fractional $p$-Laplace equation of the form $(-\Delta_p)^s u=f$ where $p>1, s\in (0, 1)$ and $f\in L^\infty_{\rm loc}(\Omega)$. Specifically, we prove that $u\in C^{0, \gamma_\circ}_{\rm loc}(\Omega)$ for $\gamma_\circ=\min\{1, \frac{sp}{p-1}\}$, provided that $\frac{sp}{p-1}\neq 1$. In particular, it shows that $u$ is locally Lipschitz for $\frac{sp}{p-1}>1$. Moreover, we show that for $\frac{sp}{p-1}=1$, the solution is locally Lipschitz, provided that $f$ is locally H\"{o}lder continuous. Additionally, we discuss further regularity results for the fractional double-phase problems.

papers.title: Mixed Local-Nonlocal Equations in the Hyperbolic Space and Sharp Sobolev Constants
papers.abstract: This paper explores the existence of solutions to a class of nonlinear elliptic equations involving a mixed local-nonlocal operator of the form $-\Delta_{\mathbb{B}^N} + (-\Delta_{\mathbb{B}^N})^s$, with $0 < s < 1$, set in the hyperbolic space. By employing variational methods, we address both subcritical and critical nonlinearities, establishing the existence of weak solutions under appropriate conditions. We also compare the best Sobolev constants for the mixed and local operators on $\mathbb{B}^N$ with the Euclidean Sobolev constant.

papers.title: An inductive approach to stochastic estimates for the $\varphi^{4}_2$-equation with correlated coefficient fields
papers.abstract: We develop an inductive approach to obtain stochastic estimates for singular SPDEs when the coefficient field is correlated with the driving noise. We implement our method, in the whole space, on the example of the $\varphi^{4}_2$-equation. Our approach is based on (infinite-dimensional) integration by parts with respect to Wick products of Gaussian random variables (more precisely, mollifications of space-time white noise) together with an inductive scheme over the moment's exponent.

papers.title: The Neumann problem for the fractional Laplacian: optimal regularity via the Mellin transform
papers.authors: Serena Dipierro, Xavier Ros-Oton, Enrico Valdinoci, Marvin Weidner
papers.abstract:
We establish the optimal regularity of solutions to the Neumann problem for the fractional Laplacian, $(-\Delta)^s u=h$ in $\Omega$, with the external condition $\mathcal N^s u=0$ in $\Omega^c$. For this, a key point is to establish a 1D Liouville theorem for functions with growth, which we prove by using complex analysis and the Mellin transform.
  More precisely, we prove a ``meta-theorem'' relating the classification of 1D solutions to general linear homogeneous equations of the type $Lu=0$ in $(0,\infty)$ to the (complex) roots of an explicit meromorphic function $f(z)$ that depends on $L$. In case of the fractional Laplacian with Neumann conditions, we show that all solutions are $C^{2s+\alpha}$ when $s\leq 1/2$, and $C^{s+\frac12+\alpha}$ when $s\geq1/2$.
  Moreover, quite surprisingly, we prove that even in 1D there exist highly oscillating solutions of the type $u(x)=x^{a} \cos(b \log x)$ for $x>0$, with $a>0$ and $b>0$ that depend on $s$, and $a<2s$ for $s\sim1$.

papers.title: Derivation of the Boltzmann equation from hard-sphere dynamics (after Y. Deng, Z. Hani, and X. Ma)
papers.authors: Thierry Bodineau, Isabelle Gallagher, Laure Saint-Raymond, Sergio Simonella
papers.abstract: Consider a microscopic system of $N$ hard spheres that are initially independent (modulo the exclusion condition on particle positions) and identically distributed in $\mathbb{R}^3$. When the number $N$ of particles goes to infinity and the diameter $\varepsilon$ of the particles goes to zero, and under the weak density assumption $N\varepsilon^2=1$, it has been known since the work of Lanford that the empirical measure for the particles converges to the solution of the Boltzmann equation in a short time interval. In particular, the particles remain dynamically independent, in this limit and in the short time interval where the correlations induced by their collisions remain under control. In a recent work, Y. Deng, Z. Hani and X. Ma successfully obtained the same convergence result in arbitrary large time; more precisely, the convergence result holds for any time interval on which the Boltzmann equation has a regular solution. In this note, we explain a few elements of their proof.

papers.title: A direct method for doubly nonlinear equations via convexification in spaces of measures and duality
papers.authors: Alessandro Pinzi, Filippo Riva, Giuseppe Savar\'e
papers.abstract:
Existence of solutions to doubly nonlinear equations in reflexive Banach spaces is established by resorting to a global-in-time variational approach inspired by De Giorgi's principle, which characterizes the associated flows as null-minimizers of a suitable energy-dissipation functional defined on trajectories. In contrast to the celebrated minimizing movements scheme, the proposed strategy does not rely on any time-discretization or iterative constructions. Instead, it provides a direct method based on the relaxation of the problem in spaces of measures, constrained by the continuity equation: in this procedure, no gap is introduced due to the Ambrosio's superposition principle.
  Within this weak convex framework, the validity of the null-minimization property is recovered through two further steps. First, a careful application of the Von Neumann minimax theorem yields an identification of the dual problem as a supremum over the set of smooth and bounded cylinder functions, solving an Hamilton-Jacobi-type inequality. Secondly, a suitable "backward boundedness" property of solutions to such Hamilton-Jacobi system gives a proper bound of the dual problem, ensuring that the minimum value of the original functional is actually zero.
  The proposed strategy naturally extends to non-autonomous equations, encompassing time- and space-dependent dissipation potentials and time-dependent potential energies.

papers.title: Liouville phenomenon for the Klein-Gordon equation in 1+1 dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the Klein-Gordon equation in one spatial and one temporal dimension. Physically, this equation describes the wave function of a relativistic spinless boson with positive rest mass. Mathematically, this is the most elementary hyperbolic partial differential equation, after the wave equation itself. Relative to the origin, the spacetime splits according to the light cones, and we find four quarter-planes, two of which are timelike while the remaining two are spacelike. Not unexpectedly, the solutions behave quite differently in the two types of quarter-planes. It turns out that the spacelike quarter-planes exhibit a Liouville phenomenon, where insufficient growth forces the solutions to display a certain kind of symmetry, where the values on the two linear edges are in a one-to-one relation. This phenomenon shares features with the classical Liouville theorem as well as the Phragmen-Lindelof principle for harmonic functions. We obtain sharp transition from uniqueness to nonuniqueness.

papers.title: Ergodicity for a Constantin-Lax-Majda-DeGregorio model of turbulent flow
papers.authors: Shunsuke Fujita, Reika Fukuizumi, Takashi Sakajo
papers.abstract: This paper presents a mathematical analysis of a one-dimensional model of turbulence based on a stochastic generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda-DeGregorio (gCLMG) equation. We focus on the specific case where the nonlinearity in the equation allows the existence of the anomalous enstrophy cascade, which is an inviscid conserved quantity, and some effective energy estimates for mathematical analysis. The existence of an invariant measure in the attractor is proved via the classical Krylov-Bogoliubov argument. The uniqueness of the measure and exponential mixing are proved under a sufficiently large viscosity condition, in which the nonlocal structure of the nonlinear term plays a prominent role. The construction of this invariant measure is the first step towards a theoretical understanding of turbulent phenomena that cause anomalous cascades in the zero viscous limit, viewed from the dynamical systems theory.

papers.title: Magnetic uncertainty in variable geometry
papers.authors: Luca Fanelli, Yilin Song, Ying Wang, Jiqiang Zheng, Ruihan Zhou
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study Hardy-type uncertainty principles and unique continuation properties for linear covariant Schrodinger equations with variable coefficients in the presence of bounded electric and magnetic potentials. Under suitable smallness assumptions on the leading coefficients, we prove that any solution exhibiting super-quadratic exponential decay at two distinct times must vanish identically. Under an additional structural assumption on the coefficient matrix $G$, we further establish a Hardy-type result at the quadratic exponential scale. We also obtain an analogous uniqueness result for the heat equation with variable-coefficient magnetic perturbations.
  Our results unify and extend previous works in two directions: they recover the constant-coefficient covariant case treated by Barcelo-Fanelli-Gutierrez-Ruiz-Vilela when $G=I$, and the variable-coefficient non-magnetic case considered by Federico-Li-Yu when $A=0$. The proofs combine logarithmic convexity arguments with Carleman estimates adapted to variable-coefficient covariant Schr\"odinger and parabolic flows. Although our approach follows the general strategy introduced by Escauriaza-Kenig-Ponce-Vega, substantial new difficulties arise from the interaction between the variable metric and the magnetic structure, which requires new weight functions and refined commutator estimates.

papers.title: Uniqueness of the dissipative SQG without time-continuity assumption
papers.abstract: We consider the uniqueness of the solution of the dissipative surface quasi-geostrophic equation, without assuming time-continuity and smallness of the solutions. We show that the uniqueness holds in the scale-critical Lebesgue spaces and non-homogeneous Besov spaces. The proof is based on the energy method, inspired by the approach introduced by Lions and Masmoudi (2001) in the study of uniqueness for the Navier-Stokes equations. A key ingredient of the argument is the justification of the energy inequality via the smoothing effect of the fractional heat semigroup together with an iteration scheme based on the structure of the integral equation.

papers.title: $L^2$-contraction and asymptotic stability of Cahn-Hilliard fronts
papers.abstract: We study the stability of transition fronts for the one-dimensional Cahn-Hilliard equation. More precisely, we prove that for any H\"older initial datum sufficiently close to a front in the $L^2$ norm, the corresponding solution of the Cahn-Hilliard equation exists globally and converges, up to a dynamical shift, to the front as time tends to infinity. The result holds for a class of double-well potentials in a $C^4$-neighborhood of the standard quartic potential. For the proof, we develop an $L^2$-stability framework adapted to Cahn-Hilliard fronts. The key ingredient is a nontrivial second-order Poincar\'e-type inequality that reveals a coercive structure in the indefinite quadratic energy form associated with the linearized operator about the front, once the dynamical shift is taken into account. This yields an $L^2$-contraction estimate and, via a far-field semigroup argument, asymptotic orbital stability of the front in the unweighted $L^2$ topology. The stability analysis requires only the $L^2$-smallness of the initial perturbation; no higher-order smallness, spatial localization, or moment assumptions are imposed.

papers.title: Unique continuation at infinity for potentials with arbitrary radial growth
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be any given continuous positive function on $\mathbb{R}_+$. Let $V$ be radial with $|V(x)|\leq G(|x|)$. We prove a Landis-type theorem for any real-valued solution of $\Delta u=Vu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We construct a decay threshold $e^{-g(r)}$, where $g$ is a strictly increasing function which can be computed explicitly in terms of $G$. Under suitable assumptions the exponent in the decay threshold is proportional to the Agmon distance associated with $G$.

papers.title: A note on p-harmonic measure
papers.abstract: Let $1 < p < \infty$. We identify the optimal decay exponent of the $p$-harmonic measure $\omega_p ( B( \xi, t) \cap \partial \mathbb{B}, 0, \mathbb{B}) $ for small $t$, where $\mathbb{B}$ is the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $\xi \in \partial \mathbb{B}$ and $B(\xi, t)$ denotes the euclidean ball centered at $\xi$ of radius $t$. As a consequence and, under suitable geometrical restrictions on a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n $, we identify the optimal decay exponent of $\omega_p ( B( \xi, t) \cap \partial \Omega, a, \Omega)$ for small $t$, where $a \in \Omega$ and $\xi \in \partial \Omega$. When restricted to the range $1 < p < n$ we provide new estimates complementing previous results of different authors in the unit ball, the unit disc or the upper half-space.

papers.title: Critical semilinear damped wave equations beyond moduli of continuity
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for semilinear classical damped wave equations with general nonnegative nondecreasing nonlinearities, without imposing a modulus-of-continuity structure or convexity. A Dini-type condition expressed directly in terms of the nonlinearity gives small data global in-time existence and extends the nonlinear framework of Ebert--Girardi--Reissig [Math. Ann. 378 (2020), 1311--1326]. When this integral diverges and the effective total mass of the initial data is positive, convergence of the Keller--Osserman tail integral is necessary and sufficient for finite-time Sobolev blow-up. Its divergence gives global grow-up under the same near-zero and mass assumptions.

papers.title: Plane wave representations for wave scattering on a sphere
papers.authors: Valentin D. Kunz, Andrey V. Shanin, Raphael C. Assier
papers.abstract: Motivated by three-dimensional wave diffraction by conical shapes, we consider the two-dimensional problem of wave scattering on the real sphere $\mathcal{S}^2$ resulting from a point-source incidence on a scatterer $\mathbb{S}$. Using the recently introduced notion of plane waves on $\mathcal{S}^2$ as well as recent results on the Laplace--Beltrami Green's function $G$ on $\mathcal{S}^2$, we derive three plane-wave representations for the scattered field $u$. We then explain how $u$ can be analytically continued to the complexified sphere $\mathcal{S}^2_{\mathbb{c}}$. This allows us to formulate a complexified version of Green's third identity, and to provide a characterisation of complex sources. All our results are then used to draw strong analogies between planar and spherical scattering problems, notably through the introduction of directivities.

papers.title: Radial pressureless Euler flow: structure and stability of absorption at the origin
papers.authors: Gaowei Cao, Feimin Huang, Guirong Tang
papers.abstract:
We study absorption at the origin in radial pressureless Euler flow in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq2$. For rotation-invariant nonnegative locally finite initial mass and bounded radial initial velocity vanishing at the origin, we prove global existence and uniqueness in a full-space radial entropy class with a one-sided Lipschitz bound and an initial kinetic-energy trace. Absorption is permanent, including retention of any initial origin atom.
  For finite positive mass with finite second moment, a Lagrangian projection representation characterizes the absorbed mass and its left limits at positive times through extreme minimizers of a free-position primitive. We derive a radial scalar momentum balance with a nonnegative Stieltjes boundary impulse measure. The minimum value of the same primitive yields a weighted Stieltjes identity equating accumulated time-weighted impulse with the integral of initial radii over absorbed labels, valid also for jumps and singular continuous absorption; the boundary impulse measure and the absorption measure are mutually absolutely continuous on $(0,\infty)$.
  For such finite-mass data with common total mass, strong $L^2$ convergence of initial quantiles and Lagrangian velocities, together with convergence of initial origin masses, yields convergence of absorbed mass at continuity times of the limiting absorption and local weak convergence of absorption measures on $(0,\infty)$. Finally, even with a fixed smooth initial radial probability density, every probability measure compactly supported in $(0,\infty)$ can be realized as the absorption measure by choosing a bounded radial initial velocity; in particular, purely singular continuous absorption occurs.

papers.title: Statistical comparison of reconstruction methods for the inverse boundary problem of the one-dimensional wave equation
papers.abstract:
Several numerical reconstruction algorithms for the inverse boundary value problem of the 1-dimensional wave equation exist. In this paper we revisit two of them, the Sondhi-Gopinath (SG) method from 1971 and the Korpela-Lassas-Oksanen (KLO) method from 2016. Our main contribution is a systematic and statistical comparison of the performance of these two well established methods. The stability of the SG algorithm, even in practical applications, is well known. KLO has a regularisation scheme with a theoretical proof, and is an evolution of the boundary control method. Both are based on the idea of constructing solutions that are characteristic functions of a set at a given time. This similarity has been pointed out before, but no systematic comparison has been published.
  We compare the performance of the two algorithms with noisy simulated data. The application in our mind is the reconstruction of the internal cross-sectional area of a pressurised fluid pipe. The area corresponds to the first order $\partial_x$-term of the wave equation. Instead of just observing the performance on a few test cases, we generate $n=1000$ random area profiles of various smoothness levels and measurement noise up to $10\%$ of the signal energy and perform statistical tests. SG and KLO have a difference of one time-derivative in their standard boundary data, which complicates the analysis. Our results show that SG performs better in the low noise regime, and KLO with high noise. SG is easier to implement and runs faster.

papers.title: The spectrum of units of algebraic $K$-theory
papers.abstract: It is well known that the $[0,1]$ and $[0,2]$ Postnikov truncations of the units of the topological $K$-theories $\glone \KO$ and $\glone \KU$, respectively, are split, and that the splitting is provided by the ($\Z/2$-graded) line bundles. In this paper we give a similar splitting for the $[0,1]$-truncation of the units of algebraic $K$-theory, considered as a sheaf on affine schemes. A crucial step is to produce the splitting for $\glone K(\Z)$. Along the way we also give a complete calculation of the connective spectrum of strict units of $K(\Z)$ and $K(\F_\ell)$ for a prime $\ell$. Finally, we show that the units of algebraic $K$-theory do not split as a presheaf. In fact we show they do not even split pointwise.

papers.title: Topological Hochschild homology of truncated Brown-Peterson spectra II
papers.abstract: We compute topological Hochschild homology of $\mathbb{E}_3$-MU-algebra forms of the second truncated Brown-Peterson spectrum with Adams summand coefficients at $p=2$ and conditionally at arbitrary primes. We also provide a new computational tool, a variant of the Brun spectral sequence, for computing topological Hochschild homology of truncated Brown-Peterson spectra with certain coefficients. As a consequence, we show that $\mathbb{E}_3$-MU-algebra forms of truncated Brown-Peterson spectra $\mathrm{BP}\langle n\rangle$ are not Thom spectra at the prime $p=2$ for any $n\ge 2$.

papers.title: Equality of the Jellium and the Uniform Electron Gas Energies
papers.abstract: Jellium, a system of electrons in a uniform neutralizing background, and the uniform electron gas (UEG), a system of electrons with constant density and no background, are two standard models of the electron gas. We prove that the ground-state energy per unit volume of Jellium, as defined by Lieb and Narnhofer, coincides with the UEG energy defined by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer, i.e. \[ e^\hbar_{\rm Jel}(\rho_0)=e^\hbar_{\rm UEG}(\rho_0). \] This equality was previously established in the classical case by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer and independently by Cotar and Petrache.

papers.title: Free Fermion frustration-free models have zero Hall conductance
papers.authors: Sven Bachmann, Zhiqian Du, Martin Fraas
papers.abstract: We give a new proof that translation-invariant free Fermion frustration-free models have zero Hall conductance. Our proof is analytic in nature and it uses the bulk-edge correspondence. The central argument, which holds beyond the translation-invariant situation, is that in frustration-free models, edge modes cannot merge into the ground state band. We give an example of a gapped frustration-free model that is nonetheless gapless on the half-plane.

papers.title: Poisson statistics for one-dimensional Anderson--Bernoulli Schr\"odinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove Poisson local eigenvalue statistics for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators with nondegenerate Bernoulli potentials at any fixed nonzero coupling. After unfolding by the integrated density of states (IDS), the local eigenvalue process converges to a Poisson point process of unit intensity at every energy in the interior of the almost-sure spectrum. The theorem also holds for bounded nonconstant iid potentials, provided the IDS is continuous and strictly increasing near the reference energy. If the IDS also has a finite positive derivative at that energy, the usual linear normalization gives the same limit. The proof uses a phase coordinate with exact IDS drift to obtain a uniform exponential crossing law and joint Poisson counts in disjoint energy windows.

papers.title: Approach to Equilibrium in Translation-Invariant Quantum Systems: Structural Results II
papers.authors: Vojkan Jak\v{s}i\'c, Claude-Alain Pillet, Anna Szczepanek
papers.abstract:
We continue the development, started in [AHP 25 (2023), 715-749], of a structural theory of approach to equilibrium in translation-invariant quantum spin systems. Dynamical Steady States (DSS) are defined as w*-limit points of the time-averaged evolution of an initial state. We show that if a DSS is an equilibrium state of a sufficiently regular interaction, then the specific energy of this interaction is necessarily a constant of the motion. Two distinct mechanisms lead to this conclusion, one based on dynamical surface energies and the other on conservation of specific relative entropy. We conjecture that these properties hold for a natural class of interactions.
  For a DSS admitting a physical equilibrium description, the associated equilibrium states are characterized by a dynamical Gibbs variational principle: they are precisely the minimizers of the specific relative entropy from the initial state over the physical equilibrium states. The achieved minimum equals the increase of specific entropy.
  The structural theory also yields characterizations of approach to thermal equilibrium, based on two model-dependent questions: restoration of a sufficiently local thermodynamic description at large times and classification of the corresponding local constants of motion. Once locality is restored, the constants of motion determine the possible asymptotic equilibrium states. In particular, if finite-range locality is restored and the energy is the only finite-range constant of the motion, then every DSS is a thermal equilibrium state at the temperature fixed by energy conservation. The finite-time dynamical input underlying this theory is established in a companion paper.

papers.title: Dynamical Conservation Laws in Quantum Spin Systems
papers.authors: Vojkan Jak\v{s}i\'c, Claude-Alain Pillet, Anna Szczepanek
papers.abstract: We study dynamical conservation laws and the propagation of thermodynamic structure in translation-invariant lattice quantum spin systems. Using Lieb-Robinson bounds [CMP 28 (1972), 251-257] in arbitrary dimension, and Araki's bounds [CMP 14 (1969), 120-157] in dimension one, we prove conservation of the specific entropy, specific energy, and specific relative entropy under suitable assumptions on the interactions. The transported local Hamiltonians admit surface energies that vanish per unit volume in the van Hove limit, and local observables remain a core for the transported generators at every finite time. Weak Gibbsianity is preserved for sufficiently small times in arbitrary dimension and for all times in dimension one.
